- No known past medical history.
- No previous surgeries reported.
- Medications: None reported.
- Social history: Non-smoker, no alcohol or recreational drug use.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Objective:
- General: Alert and oriented, appears generally well.
- Vital signs: Not documented.

- Cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal; no murmurs or extra sounds detected.
- No cyanosis or clubbing noted.
- No other system examinations documented.
- Investigations: None performed or documented during visit.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Persistent cough:
   - Assessment: Subacute cough, likely post-infectious or upper airway cough syndrome.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Upper airway cough syndrome (postnasal drip) — possible
     - Post-infectious cough — possible
     - Asthma — possible (DDx; consistent)
     - Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) — possible (DDx; consistent)
     - Less likely: pneumonia, chronic bronchitis (not supported by transcript)
   - Investigations planned: None at present; will consider if symptoms worsen or persist beyond 8 weeks.
   - Treatment planned: Supportive care, reassurance. Patient advised to monitor symptoms and return if cough persists or worsens, or if new symptoms develop (e.g., fever, hemoptysis, shortness of breath).
   - Referrals: None indicated at this time.

●  Missing but clinically expected elements: Allergies not documented. No medication reconciliation (no medications reported). No vital signs documented.
●  No internal conflicts noted between transcript and DDx.
●  Transcript clear and easy to interpret.
